business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Physical Charter of Prilled Urea and Potassium Chloride

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Double Taxation Agreement between the Independent State of Samoa and New Zealand (2002)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus, in force 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); Companies Act 2001; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Regulations 2009; relevant directives and guidance issued by the Samoa Financial Services Authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport for each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter confirming identity and business standing
Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association (or equivalent constitutional documents) for existing corporate UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registered agent or relevant Companies House

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or tenancy agreement) for each individual UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public and issuing utility or landlord

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories must be screened against the Samoa Financial Services Authority enforcement and prohibited lists, Samoa Police and domestic anti-corruption records, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, and the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to mandatory enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring in accordance with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and FSA guidelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Financial Services Authority (FSA) Companies Registry Online Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be in English or Samoan, expressed in Roman letters. Non-Roman scripts, including Chinese characters, are not accepted for the registered legal name and must be transliterated into Roman letters. The name must include a legal suffix appropriate for an International Company, typically 'IC', 'Limited', or 'Ltd'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banking, Finance, Financial, Insurance, Assurance, Trust, Trustee, Investment, Securities, Broker, Deal, Exchange, Clearing, Asset Management, Pension, Fund
Government, Ministry, Crown, National, Municipal, Samoa, Public, Authority, Government of Samoa
University, College, Academy, Institute, Chamber of Commerce
Any word implying a connection with the Samoan Government or requiring a special license under Samoa law
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies at FSA within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection and any corrected name. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Minister responsible for Justice and Commerce within 30 days of the reconsideration decision; the Minister's decision is subject to judicial review by the Supreme Court of Samoa on procedural and legal grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered office. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa, typically at the office of a licensed registered agent. A virtual office may be used for administrative correspondence only, not as a substitute for the statutory registered office. For the wholesale fertilizer trading industry, remote operational management is permitted provided the registered office and resident agent requirements are satisfied.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% - Low to moderate risk of unannounced on-site inspection by the Samoa Financial Services Authority under risk-based supervision of the wholesale commodity trading sector, elevated relative to pure offshore holding vehicles.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per screened UBO / corporate entity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2008), Sections 6, 7, 9, 12, 18, 25, 31, and 82
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-1) together with Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Company shall maintain a stated share capital in the Memorandum, but share capital may be issued as partly paid or deferred payment; no escrow account is required under Samoan law for International Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscriber named in the application be and is hereby allotted one ordinary share against payment of the subscription amount, and that the share register be updated accordingly. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that such office shall be the Company’s principal place of business for all statutory purposes. FURTHER RESOLVED that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as first officers: [Name] as Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Resident Agent. The Directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute banking mandates, and make all filings required under the International Companies Act 1987.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registry Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via SIFA's licensed registered agent, specifying the proposed company name ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The agent will conduct a name search against the International Companies Register. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days, and the agent will obtain the name clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (prepared by registered agent)
Consent from the proposed registered agent
Copy of the proposed name clearance request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for similarity to an existing company, file a revised name application with an explanation of distinctiveness or file an appeal to the Registrar within 14 days of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent in Samoa (under SIFA supervision)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association, including the object clause authorizing wholesale trading in prilled urea and potassium chloride. The sole subscriber (or corporate subscriber by its authorized officer) executes the documents in the presence of a witness, and the first director gives written consent to act.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (drafted in English)
Consent to act as first director
Consent to act as first secretary
Registered agent's certificate of acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries the object clause or capital provisions, the registered agent will amend and re-submit the documents; no fresh filing fee is charged for ministerial corrections within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent electronically files the completed Form IC-1, the executed Memorandum and Articles, consents, and the registered agent's undertaking through the SIFA e-registry portal. The government filing fee of USD 750 (or equivalent in Samoan Tala) is paid by bank draft or electronic transfer to SIFA's official revenue account.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed)
Form IC-5 (Consent to Act as Director)
Form IC-6 (Consent to Act as Secretary)
Registered Agent's Undertaking (Form IC-3)
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a notice of defect, the registered agent has 10 business days to cure the defect. If the application is rejected, the agent may withdraw and refile with a written explanation; the fee is refunded only if the rejection was due to SIFA error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and First Board Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon verification of the application, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of the Company's existence. Immediately thereafter, the incorporator(s) or the registered agent convene the first board meeting (or adopt a written resolution) to appoint officers, adopt the registered office, approve the share allotment, and authorize banking arrangements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by SIFA)
Minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting
Share register and register of directors and secretaries
Registered office consent from the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains a clerical error, apply to the Registrar for rectification under Section 82 of the International Companies Act 1987; the Registrar will issue an amended certificate within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and Ministry of Revenue (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the registered agent appointment, updates the public register of directors (if any), and secures the Tax Identification Number (TIN) from the Ministry of Revenue for banking and customs administration. For an International Company operating under the International Companies Act 1987, income derived offshore is tax exempt; no active tax registration beyond obtaining a TIN is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (copy)
Form IC-8 (Appointment of Registered Agent)
TIN application form (to Ministry of Revenue)
Bank account opening document package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TIN application is delayed, the Ministry of Revenue may issue a temporary reference number; the registered agent will follow up and provide supporting documentation to expedite the permanent TIN.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licensing and Registration Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Wholesale Trading) — Not required for a pure offshore International Company that does not conduct physical business or invite customers within Samoa; required only if the Company establishes a physical warehouse or sales presence in Samoa.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for offshore wholesale trading of prilled urea and potassium chloride with no manufacturing, processing, or physical handling in Samoa; a 'Registration' level assessment may apply if the Company stores fertilizer at a Samoan port facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If storage occurs: fertilizer storage must be under cover to prevent run-off; wastewater/stormwater discharge must comply with Samoa's National Environmental Standards for discharge to groundwater and surface water; no open burning; no solid waste accumulation. If no physical operations, all standards remain not applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for an offshore International Company with no physical premises in Samoa. If the Company later establishes a storage or office facility, the National Building Authority (NBA) structural clearance, a Fire Safety Clearance from Samoa Fire & Emergency Services Authority, and an occupational safety inspection by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour will be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), Apia; taxpayer eFiling portal https://efiling.revenue.gov.ws/; customs clearance via Samoa Customs Service (ASYCUDA World); International Company registry administered by the Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFSC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) must apply through its licensed Samoan registered agent by lodging the TIN registration form with the Ministry for Revenue together with: certificate of incorporation, memorandum & articles, IC operating licence issued by SIFSC, particulars of the registered office/agent in Samoa, and beneficial ownership declarations. The Ministry issues a single Business TIN within 5 business days; separate VAGST registration (VAGST number) must be obtained where annual taxable supplies reach WST 100,000. ICs engaged exclusively in offshore wholesale (sale of urea and potash to non-residents) require no income-tax registration and no minimum capital import.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — the Samoa International Company is statutorily exempt (International Companies Act 1987, ss.125-127) from income tax, VAGST on offshore supplies, stamp duty, estate duty and gift duty for 20 years from incorporation; a flat annual government licence fee applies in lieu of income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box classification regime. The available elections are: (i) re-domestication/continuance of an IC as a domestic company (becoming assessable at Samoa's 27% corporate income tax rate and VAGST at 15%) or of a domestic company as an IC (obtaining the 20-year exempt-zone status); and (ii) VAGST voluntary registration to obtain input credits on exports. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are curtailed by statutory anti-avoidance rules (Income Tax Act 2012, ss.99-100).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — GST-type consumption tax under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1994.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month rolling period; entities making solely zero-rated export supplies (e.g., urea and potash sold to non-resident buyers) may register voluntarily to claim refunds of input VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous e-invoicing mandate. VAGST-registered businesses must issue compliant tax invoices (VAGST Act 1994, s.29) and file returns electronically via the Ministry for Revenue eFiling portal. All export consignments of fertilizers are cleared through the ASYCUDA World customs platform using the Single Goods Declaration; no additional fiscal seal or clearance API applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAGST) is available for goods physically exported from Samoa within the statutory window under VAGST Act 1994 s.17, for international freight and for qualifying supplies to non-residents; for an exempt-zone IC, offshore wholesale turnover of prilled urea and potassium chloride is entirely outside Samoa's VAGST tax base, resulting in a 0% effective charge with no VAGST payable and credit entitlement for input tax attributable to export supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Goods Declaration (SGD) – customs export declaration lodged in ASYCUDA World with customs-certified exit
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal of urea/potash from Samoa
Commercial Invoice and packing list matching the declared commodity (HS 3102 urea; HS 3104 potassium chloride)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank credit advice evidencing receipt of foreign currency from the non-resident buyer
Copy of IC licence and TIN certificate for exporter identification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are audited by the Ministry for Revenue for up to 5 years (unlimited on fraud) and may be clawed back with interest. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 rise from 20% (lack of reasonable care) to 40% (recklessness), 100% (intentional disregard) and 150% (evasion), plus a 2% monthly late-payment penalty and prosecution fines/imprisonment for fraudulent VAGST refund claims. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days breaches the Exchange Control Regulations 1974 and can trigger Central Bank of Samoa monetary penalties and debt action in addition to the VAT clawback; sham export documentation also triggers criminal prosecution under the Crimes Act 2016.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and the designated authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1977. CBS licenses and supervises authorised dealer banks, administers the Samoa Tala (WST) managed-float currency system, and issues all exchange-control permits and foreign-currency account approvals.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: WST is a non-internationally-traded, managed-float currency; convertibility is administered through authorised dealer commercial banks. Current-account transactions (trade in goods, services, and routine profit remittances) are broadly liberalised, requiring only CBS-prescribed EC forms submitted via the receiving/remitting bank. Capital-account transactions, including equity injections by non-residents and cross-border financing, require CBS approval or an exemption. For a Samoa International Company (IC), the International Companies Act 1987 (s.204) exempts the IC from the Exchange Control Act 1976 for any transaction denominated in a foreign currency and involving no Samoan-resident counterparty; therefore the IC's USD-denominated capital injections, charter proceeds, and profit remittances are not subject to WST conversion or CBS prior-approval where the funds do not transit a Samoan bank account. Where funds do pass through a Samoan bank, the bank applies EC-1/EC-4 filings and CBS balance-of-payments reporting, but no convertibility restriction is imposed if the account is designated as a non-resident foreign-currency account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Samoan resident exporter, CBS rules require (i) full repatriation of export proceeds through an authorised dealer within 3 months of shipment (extendable to 6 months with CBS consent), and (ii) mandatory conversion to WST of 100% of repatriated proceeds unless a CBS-approved foreign-currency retention account is held with an authorised dealer. A Samoa IC conducting an offshore physical charter trade in prilled urea and potassium chloride (ISIC 4669) is a non-resident for exchange-control purposes under the International Companies Act 1987 s.204; consequently the statutory mandatory-conversion ratio is 0% for foreign-currency receipts retained offshore. The IC may hold USD proceeds freely in its offshore treasury account; if the IC ever books export proceeds into Samoa, the bank will treat the IC as a non-resident and apply the retention-account protocol rather than the 100% surrender rule, provided the EC-4 declaration and IC certificates are lodged.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Samoa has no statutory framework for fintech e-money institutions (EMIs), no sandbox, and no domestic EMI licence class; a Samoa IC cannot obtain local e-money authorisation. Offshore EMIs (EEA/Singapore/HK licensed) may in principle hold funds for the IC, but most mainstream platforms decline Samoa-IC clients due to enhanced-risk classification and opaque beneficial-ownership optics. EMIs are therefore viable only for immaterial operational expenses (sub-USD 5,000 per item) and cannot serve as the primary clearing rail for fertilizer trade settlements or LC operations. The strategic posture is to run the primary treasury at a regulated international correspondent bank outside Samoa and use no Samoan domestic clearing for the offshore charter trades.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in Samoa to open an account. A Samoa IC may be onboarded remotely subject to: (i) a licensed registered agent (TCSP) in Apia issuing the statutory Introductory Letter; (ii) director/shareholder identification certified by a lawyer or accountant in the individual's home jurisdiction; (iii) beneficial-ownership verification per the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; and (iv) compliance sign-off on a video-conference interview with the bank's AML officer, which is the uniform internal policy of ANZ and BSP. In practice, for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced agrochemical commodity trader, ANZ/BSP may escalate the file to regional credit or require a joint interview at the bank's Apia office; a board resolution appointing the TCSP as liaison for KYC meetings eliminates the need for any director to travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore IC with nominee or absentee directors and no operating substance in Samoa flagged under beneficial-ownership rules and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; Certificate of Incumbency from the licensed registered agent naming all directors, shareholders, and nominees; signed nominee acknowledgement declarations; CBS-compliant Beneficial Ownership Declaration Form identifying ultimate natural persons; certified passports; and a substance narrative demonstrating that board meetings are held by phone/video under the IC Act and that the registered agent maintains corporate records in Apia.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: TBML red flags in high-value fertilizer trades: over/under-invoicing, phantom shipments, price volatility creating mismatch between contract and invoice.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction trade pack containing: (a) signed sale/purchase contract with Incoterms 2020; (b) commercial invoice matching contract price and grade; (c) third-party inspection certificates (SGS/Intertek) for weight, urea content, and potash grade; (d) Bill of Lading and, where chartering, the charter party or vessel nomination; (e) payment instructions with proper CBS/ISO purpose codes; (f) quarterly independent reconciliation of physical cargo documents versus payment flows prepared by the TCSP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions alert triggered by Russian/Belarusian-origin urea or potash producers, trading counterparties, or flagged vessels on the LC or wire instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counsel opinion confirming no UN/EU/US OFAC/CBS sanctioned party in the chain; producer certificates of origin; end-user certificates; vessel tracking and transshipment records confirming no embargoed-port calls; contractual Sanctions Clause, Withdrawal Clause, and warranty that cargo will not be re-supplied to sanctioned jurisdictions; enhanced due diligence on the consignee and confirmation of no dual-use concerns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection sourced from a private-wealth or multi-layer holding vehicle where the provenance of equity is unverified, blocking first-cargo funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder source-of-wealth dossier: audited financial statements for the last two years; board resolution authorizing the capital injection; bank statement trail from the originating account demonstrating salary/divestiture/inheritance provenance; SWIFT MT103 or MT202 evidencing the inbound equity remittance; and a written declaration that funds are not derived from proceeds of crime or political-exposed persons linked to Samoan or foreign public office.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity as a USD wire via SWIFT MT103 with ISO purpose code 'G2' (equity injection) or, where the Samoan bank requires EC-4 classification, 'K – Equity Capital'. The IC should maintain the primary treasury account offshore (e.g., a New York or Hong Kong USD account of a prime correspondent bank) to keep the capital outside CBS formality. If the injection must transit a Samoan authorised dealer, the bank requires: EC-1 form, board capital resolution, Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and the source-of-wealth pack, and credits a segregated 'Share Capital – Escrow' sub-account. USD clearing should be executed via Fedwire/CHIPS in New York or RTGS in Hong Kong, with the Samoa IC named exactly as per Certificate of Incorporation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for charters, port costs, and supplier instalments; (ii) Commercial Irrevocable Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) with amendments via MT707 and negotiation via MT740/MT742 for the purchase of prilled urea and potassium chloride, issued by the buyer or confirmed to the IC; (iii) documentary collections (MT400) where the counterparty relationship is established; (iv) for pure offshore trades, settlement via a non-Samoan USD account using MT202 COV to move cover between correspondent banks, avoiding the Samoan EC-5 form; (v) if goods physically transit Samoa, the bank requires EC-5 documentation and CBS-approved import/export forms, plus customs clearance through the Ministry for Revenue, reducing efficiency. The daily operating structure should segregate trade disbursements from operating expenses across two sub-accounts to preserve audit clarity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla USD/WST forward contracts with authorised dealer banks (ANZ, BSP) for maturities up to 12 months, used only for WST operating-cost hedges; liquidity is thin and non-trade forwards require CBS approval.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) executed with a licensed bank subject to CBS notification, practically limited to matched capital-flow or interest-rate hedging; not used for speculative positions.

USD-denominated commodity derivative contracts traded offshore — ICE/CME urea and potash swaps, plain-vanilla options, and exchange-cleared futures — permissible and outside Samoan exchange control because the IC maintains the treasury account offshore and transacts in foreign currency under International Companies Act 1987 s.204.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST are not available in any recognised international market; the IC should instead denominate all charter and trade contracts in USD to eliminate WST conversion exposure at the structural level.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Government Licence Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour / Samoa International Finance Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month or part thereof; unpaid fees for six consecutive months may result in administrative strike-off without prior notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987; no statutory audit triggered by revenue, assets, or ownership unless the company's articles so require or a third-party lender mandates a certified audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for voluntary financial statements; no prescribed local GAAP for International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return date the registered agent must confirm and certify the register of members (including any share transfers), directors, secretary, registered office, and ultimate beneficial owners. A signed declaration by the UBO or shareholder must be obtained and retained in the company records. Any share transfer during the year must be filed in the Register of Members prior to the annual confirmation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: None required; USD 1,500 - USD 3,500 if voluntarily engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified Samoa International Company (IC) is exempt from Samoan income tax, yielding an effective corporate income tax rate of 0% on non-Samoa-source income. No capital gains tax applies. Export supplies of physical goods are generally outside the net of Samoa VAGST.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Ministry of Revenue Form CITR-1); electronic filing through Samoa Ministry of Revenue e-Services portal. A tax-exempt International Company is outside the active CIT return filing system and instead maintains annual filings with the Samoa International Financial Authority.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No CIT filing deadline applies to an exempt International Company. For a taxable resident company, the return is due within six months of the financial year-end, normally 31 March or the selected balance date approved by the Ministry of Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, including legal name, tax registration number, and International Company licence number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempt IC should enter its International Company registration number and attach the tax exemption confirmation. No taxable income line should be completed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Samoan sources. For exempt ICs, this amount is nil unless the IC has carried on business within Samoa or with a Samoa resident other than as expressly permitted under the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accurately identify and disclose any Samoan-source trading, service, or charter income; incorrect nil reporting risks loss of the tax exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and allowable losses. For an exempt IC, allocation of expenditure is not required for CIT purposes but must be contemporaneously documented for economic substance and transfer-pricing review.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare a functional and economic substance file showing physical procurement, broker, and freight activities outside Samoa if no Samoan taxable income is reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed at the 27% headline rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter zero and cite the International Company statutory exemption; do not claim deductions as an alternative to using the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Self-assessed tax payable, tax credits, and status of withholding payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempt IC has no self-assessed Samoan CIT liability. Maintain a reconciliation of any Samoan-sourced payments subject to potential withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file by a taxable company may trigger immediate late return penalties, late payment penalties of 10% of the unpaid tax, daily continuing surcharges, and assessment action by the Ministry of Revenue. For an exempt IC, failure to maintain SIFA annual filings risks licence revocation and statutory monetary penalties under the International Companies Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an exempt International Company. For a resident company not falling within the IC regime, the statutory dividend withholding tax rate is 15% for non-resident shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa has a limited double tax treaty network, primarily focused on tax information exchange and avoidance of income tax on certain cross-border payments. To invoke treaty-based relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home jurisdiction and file the Ministry of Revenue relief application with the payer before the payment date. For an exempt International Company, no dividend withholding tax arises, and no treaty relief application is necessary for dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For ordinary Samoan resident companies, the domestic withholding tax rates are 15% for interest and 15% for royalties. Treaty relief may reduce these rates subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership evidence. Payments of interest and royalties by an exempt International Company are not subject to Samoan withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A - Samoa has not prescribed a statutory Local File or Master File threshold as of 2025. However, transactions between an IC and any Samoa-resident associated enterprise must comply with the arm's length principle, and the Ministry of Revenue may make transfer-pricing adjustments. Responsible practice is to maintain TP documentation when annual related-party transactions exceed WST 10 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's international company legislation incorporates economic substance requirements to counter harmful tax practices. An IC engaged in relevant activities, including distribution and service centre operations, must demonstrate adequate physical presence, qualified personnel, and core income-generating activities in Samoa. Annual economic substance declarations must be filed with the Samoa International Financial Authority. The wholesale charter and physical supply of urea and potash will be scrutinised as a distribution and service activity; failure to demonstrate substance in Samoa or in a comparable qualifying jurisdiction may result in penalties and loss of the tax exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false or misleading returns with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, knowingly underdeclaring Samoan-source income, or fraudulently claiming International Company tax exemption while conducting a taxable Samoan business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 7 years and monetary fines of up to WST 100,000, with additional tax equal to 100% of the evaded amount; further administrative penalties and surcharges apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally and jointly liable for unpaid taxes and penal tax where they knowingly participated in false returns; travel bans and director disqualification orders can also be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company solely as a pass-through invoicing vehicle for urea and potash trades without personnel, premises, records, or board decision-making in Samoa, and without meeting the relevant-activity substance obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties, deregistration, dissemination of the International Company licence, and potential inclusion in international harmful-tax blacklists; SIFA may impose fines and require remedial substance steps.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced; directors can be made personally liable for aggregate tax losses to Samoa, prohibited from acting as directors for a defined period, and subjected to civil recovery actions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing large Swift LC and wire-transfer payments for fertilizer cargoes without customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions screening, or transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Samoa's AML/CFT regime, freezing orders, closure of bank accounts, and revocation of the International Company registration; beneficial-ownership reporting breaches carry separate monetary penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal civil penalties, criminal prosecution where money laundering is proven, and imprisonment of up to 10 years; assets can be restrained or confiscated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Interposing a related-party shell entity to inflate the purchase price of urea or potassium chloride, shift profit out of the tax net, or otherwise circumvent Samoa revenue laws; or executing back-to-back paper transactions lacking commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the arrangement, recharacterisation under Samoa's anti-avoidance rules, assessment to Samoan tax at 27%, plus late-payment penalties and statutory interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or approve artificial intermediary structures face personal liability for the additional tax and interest, and criminal sanctions if the arrangement is prosecuted as tax fraud.
